reason: The image-only reading left the abbreviations, the damaged lines and the rubric boundaries uncertain; the edition fixed the expansions and the sequence, and showed that the text runs from the pencil 'v' side to the 'r' side.
sources: Robert Steele (ed.), Secretum secretorum cum glossis et notulis, Opera hactenus inedita Rogeri Baconi fasc. V (Oxford, 1920), pp. 109-120, archive.org operahactenusine05baco (page images pp. 109, 114-120; p. 110 footnote on OCR only)
text:
Source-assisted reading of Stams, Frg. 234 (F-2ma4), made with Steele's edition of the Secretum secretorum (1920), pp. 109-120, available. A research reader reread on the native images: canvas 1 col a (boxes 2950,400,4200,1500 and 2850,3320,4150,4140), canvas 1 col b (boxes 4150,400,5450,1500 and 4150,2900,5450,4140), canvas 0 col a lines 1-12 (box 2760,400,4020,1300) and canvas 0 col b lines 1-27 (boxes 3980,400,5140,1500 and 3980,1400,5140,2400). A second research reader read canvas 0 col a lines 13-25 (box 2760,1330,3980,2250) and the later inscription (box 4380,2750,5250,4250). Other lines rest on the image-only first reading. Text order: canvas 1 before canvas 0. Expansions in parentheses; ? = uncertain; [..] = lost or unread; [x] = supplied.
